text:
ben.davis: Seeing a bunch of customer reports where requests from their proxy are being routed to EU instead of US. Latency spikes and extra cross-region egress billing.

kate.support: Customer sent sample headers — looks mostly normal but one header has an odd character. attaching sample.

ben.davis: sample header they sent: `X-Client-Region: us-west\u0000` (they say their proxy adds a NUL). When that goes through our edge it seems to drop the header entirely and router falls back to nearest-pop (eu-west for that request).

mike.sre: if the header is present but contains a null byte, our front proxy (nginx variant) may treat it as header termination and drop it. Can you paste curl repro?

ben.davis: repro curl they used: `curl -v -H $'X-Client-Region: us-west\x00' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate` — customer says their internal proxy appends `\x00` as a placeholder.

andrew.runtime: interesting — our routing logic checks for header existence + non-empty string. If proxy strips header earlier, router never sees it. Could be LB sanitization.

elena.net: I pulled edge logs for one of the affected requests: `edge-1234 - - [17/Mar/2026:09:12:45 +0000] "POST /v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 200 234 - "X-Client-Region:"` header missing. Upstream from customer shows header with trailing null.

ingress-bot: New alert created: #INC-2026-412 region-routing-misroute (assigned to eng-net).

kate.support: Customer impact: intermittent cross-region latency (~250-400ms extra) and unexpected egress charges. They want a mitigation ASAP.

mike.sre: Quick mitigation ideas: 1) Ask customer to URL param `?region=us-west` or set `X-Region-Override` header without null. 2) Add temporary router rule to honor query param priority over header. 3) Add ingress rewrite to strip NULs (but careful).

andrew.runtime: I prefer router rule to prioritize explicit query param -- low risk and fast. I'll open a canary rollout for 2% of traffic for requests that match `region=` query param.

ben.davis: Customer can't easily change proxy today. They asked for us to accept their current header. Any chance we can detect the NUL and treat it as present but trimmed?

mike.sre: Our proxy stack currently rejects headers containing control chars. Some components strip them as part of header parsing (this is why header disappears). We could add a targeted ingress filter that treats `X-Client-Region` specially and maps `us-west\x00` to `us-west` if present in upstream raw bytes. Needs careful rollout.

elena.net: I've captured raw tcp dump from edge -> upstream for one sample. The raw header bytes contain `75 73 2d 77 65 73 74 00` which is `us-west\0`. The TLS termination (our LB) appears to normalize and drop control bytes, ending up with empty header on the downstream side.

andrew.runtime: Summary: loss happens at LB/TLS termination layer. Fix options: 1) LB config to preserve bytes (unlikely due to security rules), 2) add early ingress that reads raw bytes before TLS termination (not feasible), 3) ask customer to stop sending NUL, or 4) prioritize query param / alternate header.

kate.support: I'll escalate to customer with workaround to use `?region=us-west` or set `X-Region-Override: us-west` (no NUL). Also offering to help patch their proxy.

ben.davis: Customer wants a server-side patch instead. Can we provide a short-term mitigation?

mike.sre: We can add a router rule: if `X-Client-Region` is missing but `X-Client-Region-raw` exists (some proxies forward raw headers differently), or if `region` query param present, route accordingly. I'll get a ticket and a 48h patch. Low blast canary first.

andrew.runtime: Created PR to add query-param precedence and a small mapping rule for `X-Region-Override`. Will canary to US edge only. PR link: https://git.redwood/infra/router/merge-req/789

ingress-bot: Deploy job started for canary policy (job-4567).

elena.net: Note for long-term: SDKs should sanitize header values to remove control chars before sending. File an SDK issue.

kate.support: I'll include SDK recommendation in the support note. Also customer is being offered a temporary exemption to manual billing review for cross-region charges until we have mitigation.

ben.davis: Thanks. Keep me posted.

mike.sre: Update: canary deployed to us-east-1 edge. After ~30m we see 0 misroutes for traffic that used `?region=`. Still seeing some misroutes from customers who can't add param.

andrew.runtime: Next: create small inbound header rewriting rule in edge that if raw header contained common suffix NUL pattern (we can only detect in signed logs), try fallback mapping. This is risky — need security review.

elena.net: Filed infra ticket INFRA-2212 for header-sanitization with security tag.

kate.support: Customer accepted query-param workaround for now. They will work on proxy patch and we'll revisit after INFRA-2212.

ben.davis: Closing this thread for now. If anyone sees recurrence open a new thread and ping me. :thumbsup:
